own_solution.law: Ideal entropy of mixing at equal T and p: dS = -R sum n_i ln x_i (each gas expands isothermally from V_i = x_i V to V)
assumptions: insulated rigid container so T stays constant for ideal mixing

defect_reasons.missing_assumption: For the R sentences, helium let into a compartment of an insulated container receives flow work (and the sliding partition compresses the argon), so strictly the gases would not stay at one common temperature unless that is assumed; the intended reading (2.8 mol He at the common T and p) is the natural one.

notes: Base: x_He = 1.5/4 = 0.375, x_Ar = 0.625. dS = 8.314 x (1.5 x 0.98083 + 2.5 x 0.47000) = 8.314 x 2.64625 = 22.001 J/K. With 1.3 mol more He in the helium compartment (common T and p kept, partition slides): x_He = 2.8/5.3 = 0.52830, x_Ar = 0.47170; dS = 8.314 x (2.8 x 0.63809 + 2.5 x 0.75142) = 8.314 x 3.66518 = 30.472 J/K. Volume cancels because V_i/V = n_i/n at equal T and p -> C. Balloon has no tube to the container -> D. Earlier-run sentences describe a past event -> D. TA337 and TA9C4 state 'a small amount' with no number. The flagged temperature issue concerns only the R sentences and I judge it medium because 'at the temperature of the gases' is naturally read as leaving the common temperature unchanged.
